sentence_stem: Tom has never visited London, so
correct_completion: he wants to go there next year.
full_sentence: Tom has never visited London, so he wants to go there next year.
acceptable_variants: he plans to visit it next year.
he would love to see it someday.

options.why_wrong: This contradicts 'has never visited'. The present perfect with 'never' means the experience did not happen.

options.text: he has been there many times.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts 'has never visited'. Being there many times would mean he has visited it.

options.text: he wants to go there next year.

options.why_wrong: Living in London would mean he has visited it, which contradicts 'has never visited'.

grammar_focus: Present perfect with 'never' and the cause-effect connector 'so'
explanation: After 'so', we need a result that follows logically from the fact that Tom has never visited London. A plan to go there next year is the natural consequence.
translation: Tom nigdy nie odwiedził Londynu, więc chce tam pojechać w przyszłym roku.
